old_text:
To gather the #ICON1 {Food} resource, Citizens must build {Farms} near your cities.
One Citizen can work on each Farm. Since each city can have only five farms, you may need to
build additional cities to increase your food production.
new_text:
To gather the #ICON1 {Grub} resource, Citi-snails must build {Fern-tile Fields} near your cities.
One Citi-snail can work on each Fern-tile Field. Since each city can have only five Fern-tile Fields, you may need to
build additional cities to increase your grub production.

old_text:
Your {Library} is where your nation conducts research. Select your {Library} to research different technologies--{Military} #ICON24,
{Civics} #ICON25, {Commerce} #ICON26, and {Science} #ICON27. Each technology you research will
open up new opportunities for your nation. Once you have completed enough research the {Age} #ICON23 button
will light up, and you will be able to advance to a new Age of history.
new_text:
Your {Fossil Record} is where your nation conducts research. Select your {Fossil Record} to research different technologies--{Military} #ICON24,
{Civics} #ICON25, {Commerce} #ICON26, and {Science} #ICON27. Each technology you research will
open up new opportunities for your nation. Once you have completed enough research the {Age} #ICON23 button
will light up, and you will be able to advance to a new Age of Earth.

old_text:
Create additional {Citizens} by selecting your City and clicking the {Create Citizen} button. You can queue up several citizens to be created one at a time. If you
change your mind, you can cancel unit creation by clicking on the Citizen icon in the queue
on the right side of the screen.
new_text:
Create additional {Citi-snails} by selecting your City and clicking the {Create Citi-snail} button. You can queue up several Citi-snails to be created one at a time. If you
change your mind, you can cancel unit creation by clicking on the Citi-snail icon in the queue
on the right side of the screen.

old_text:
Move your {Scout} into the unexplored (dark) areas of the map to reveal hidden territory. Your scout
can also explore {Ruins} to gain resource bonuses and discover rare resources such as Silk,
Wine, and Horses, which Merchants from your Market can claim.
new_text:
Move your {Trackworm} into the unexplored (dark) areas of the map to reveal hidden territory. Your Trackworm
can also explore {Ruins} to gain resource bonuses and discover rare resources such as Spider Silk,
Fermented Fruit, and Wild Herds, which Milli-peddlers from your Shell Exchange can claim.

old_text:
To gather the #ICON2 {Timber} resource, build {Woodcutter's Camps} near forests. The more
trees near a Woodcutter's Camp, the more citizens will be able to work there (and the faster you will gather Timber). Gathering Timber will never "exhaust" the trees in your forests, but once
a Woodcutter's Camp is "full" of citizens you will need to build additional Woodcutter's Camps near
other forests in order to gather Timber faster.
new_text:
To gather the #ICON2 {Fernwood} resource, build {Wood-chewer's Camps} near forests. The more
trees near a Wood-chewer's Camp, the more Citi-snails will be able to work there (and the faster you will gather Fernwood). Gathering Fernwood will never "exhaust" the trees in your forests, but once
a Wood-chewer's Camp is "full" of Citi-snails you will need to build additional Wood-chewer's Camps near
other forests in order to gather Fernwood faster.

old_text:
Your {Capital} city is the political center of your nation and you must defend it at all costs.
You can eliminate an enemy nation by conquering and holding its Capital. To increase
the defenses of your Capital, consider building a Temple, Towers, and Forts. City defense also increases slightly with each additional building constructed.
new_text:
Your {Capital} city is the political center of your nation and you must defend it at all costs.
You can eliminate an enemy nation by conquering and holding its Capital. To increase
the defenses of your Capital, consider building an Amber Shrine, Stroma-towers, and Reef Forts. City defense also increases slightly with each additional building constructed.

old_text:
Your {National Borders} extend out from your cities based on the political strength of your nation.
You can normally construct new buildings only within your national territory. To increase your national
territory you must build new {Cities}, {Forts}, and {Temples}. Or, upgrade your nation's political strength
by researching #ICON25 Civics.
new_text:
Your {National Borders} extend out from your cities based on the political strength of your nation.
You can normally construct new buildings only within your national territory. To increase your national
territory you must build new {Cities}, {Reef Forts}, and {Amber Shrines}. Or, upgrade your nation's political strength
by researching #ICON25 Civics.

old_text: #ICON25 {Civic} research at the Library allows you to build additional cities; this strengthens your economy and extends your national borders.
new_text: #ICON25 {Civic} research at the Fossil Record allows you to build additional cities; this strengthens your economy and extends your national borders.

old_text:
The #ICON3 {Wealth} resource is gathered by {Caravans} trading between your cities. To trade, you will need to build at least two cities, and
then create Caravans at the {Market}. Wealth is also gathered by increasing the percentage of the world's territory you control; the more territory you have, the more taxes you receive. {Taxation} can be researched at the {Temple}.
new_text:
The #ICON3 {Shells} resource is gathered by {Roly-Poly Caravans} trading between your cities. To trade, you will need to build at least two cities, and
then create Roly-Poly Caravans at the {Shell Exchange}. Shells is also gathered by increasing the percentage of the world's territory you control; the more territory you have, the more taxes you receive. {Tax-onomy} can be researched at the {Amber Shrine}.

old_text: The level of #ICON24 {Military} technology you research at the Library determines your #ICON20 {Population Limit}, the maximum number of units your nation is allowed to control. If you reach your population limit, perform additional Military research at the Library. Military research also provides access to powerful Siege and Artillery units as well as better defensive fortifications. If you research more Military technology than you actually need for a particular unit or unit upgrade, the cost of the unit or upgrade is significantly reduced.
new_text: The level of #ICON24 {Military} technology you research at the Fossil Record determines your #ICON20 {Population Limit}, the maximum number of units your nation is allowed to control. If you reach your population limit, perform additional Military research at the Fossil Record. Military research also provides access to powerful Siege and Siege Beast units as well as better defensive fortifications. If you research more Military technology than you actually need for a particular unit or unit upgrade, the cost of the unit or upgrade is significantly reduced.

old_text:
Create military units to defend your nation against enemies. Your citizens must first build a Barracks. Select a Citizen, click the {Military Buildings}
button, click {Barracks}, and then click where you want the Barracks to be built.
new_text:
Create military units to defend your nation against enemies. Your Citi-snails must first build Burrow-acks. Select a Citi-snail, click the {Military Buildings}
button, click {Burrow-acks}, and then click where you want the Burrow-acks to be built.

old_text:
Different military units have different strengths and weaknesses. For instance, Heavy Infantry units
such as Hoplites and Phalanxes are very strong against cavalry and are useful when attacking enemy
buildings, but are highly vulnerable to attack by Bowmen and Archers. Try to use your units in ways
that take advantage of their strengths and minimize their weaknesses.
new_text:
Different military units have different strengths and weaknesses. For instance, Heavy Brawlers units
such as Worm-lites and Spine-alanx are very strong against runners and are useful when attacking enemy
buildings, but are highly vulnerable to attack by Bow-slugs and Halluci-archers. Try to use your units in ways
that take advantage of their strengths and minimize their weaknesses.

or building and then position your mouse over the {Range} icon in the lower right area of the screen.
The combat range will be drawn on the main map.
new_text:
To see the combat range of a Halluci-archer, a Stroma-tower, or another ranged unit or building, select the unit

The combat range will be drawn on the main map.

old_text:

new_text:

old_text:

new_text:

old_text:
Once you have researched four Library technologies (in a normal game) you can advance to the next {Age} by
clicking the #ICON23 {Age Advance} button at the Library. Advancing in Age will allow you to access additional
units, buildings, and technologies.
new_text:
Once you have researched four Fossil Record technologies (in a normal game) you can advance to the next {Age} by
clicking the #ICON23 {Age Advance} button at the Fossil Record. Advancing in Age will allow you to access additional
units, buildings, and technologies.

old_text:
When you have reached at least the #ICON28 Classical Age, you can begin gathering #ICON5 {Metal}, a resource useful
for building military units. To gather metal, build a {Mine} near a mountain or cliff and assign Citizens to
work there. The bigger the mountain or cliff, the more Citizens you will be able to assign. To increase your
Metal gathering, build Mines near additional mountains or cliffs.
new_text:
When you have reached at least the #ICON28 Cambrian Explosion, you can begin gathering #ICON5 {Minerals}, a resource useful
for building military units. To gather Minerals, build a {Geo-dig} near a mountain or cliff and assign Citi-snails to
work there. The bigger the mountain or cliff, the more Citi-snails you will be able to assign. To increase your
Minerals gathering, build Geo-digs near additional mountains or cliffs.

old_text: Horsemen, Knights, and other mounted units are built at the {Stable}. To build a {Stable} you must reach the #ICON28 Classical Age and research at least one #ICON24 Military technology at the Library.
new_text: Light Horse-shrimp, Ichthy-knights, and other runners are built at the {Stampede Pen}. To build a {Stampede Pen} you must reach the #ICON28 Cambrian Explosion and research at least one #ICON24 Military technology at the Fossil Record.

old_text: Build a {Granary} in a City to increase the #ICON1 {Food} output of all {Farms} in that city.
new_text: Build a {Spore-ary} in a City to increase the #ICON1 {Grub} output of all {Fern-tile Fields} in that city.

old_text: Build a {Lumber Mill} in a City to increase the #ICON2 {Timber} output of all {Woodcutter's Camps} in that city.
new_text: Build a {Timber Gnaw-mill} in a City to increase the #ICON2 {Fernwood} output of all {Wood-chewer's Camps} in that city.

old_text: Build a {Smelter} in a City to increase the #ICON5 {Metal} output of all {Mines} in that city.
new_text: Build a {Lava-smelter} in a City to increase the #ICON5 {Minerals} output of all {Geo-digs} in that city.

old_text: To attack enemy buildings such as Towers and Cities, build {Siege} and {Artillery} units at a {Siege Factory}. In order to build a Siege Factory, you must reach the #ICON28 Classical Age and research two #ICON24 Military technologies.
new_text: To attack enemy buildings such as Towers and Cities, build {Siege Beasts} at the {Rockfall Works}. In order to build a Rockfall Works, you must reach the #ICON28 Cambrian Explosion and research two #ICON24 Military technologies.

old_text: Press SHIFT while dragging a box around units to add them to your current selection. Press CTRL while dragging a box around units to select Civilian as well as Military units. Press ALT while dragging to select only non-siege military units. Press CTRL + ALT to select only siege units. Press ALT + SHIFT to select only aircraft. Press CTRL + SHIFT to select only Citizens and Scholars. Press CTRL + ALT + SHIFT to select only Transports.
new_text: Press SHIFT while dragging a box around units to add them to your current selection. Press CTRL while dragging a box around units to select Civilian as well as Military units. Press ALT while dragging to select only non-siege military units. Press CTRL + ALT to select only siege units. Press ALT + SHIFT to select only flyers. Press CTRL + SHIFT to select only Citi-snails and Bookworms. Press CTRL + ALT + SHIFT to select only Transports.

old_text: Once you have researched two #ICON26 {Commerce} technologies, you can sell excess resources at your Market, or buy needed resources. Prices will fluctuate up and down over the course of the game, so pay attention to the trends and you can maximize the efficiency of your trading.
new_text: Once you have researched two #ICON26 {Commerce} technologies, you can sell excess resources at your Shell Exchange, or buy needed resources. Prices will fluctuate up and down over the course of the game, so pay attention to the trends and you can maximize the efficiency of your trading.

old_text:
To queue several consecutive move orders, press SHIFT while clicking the destinations.
To tell a Citizen to build a series of buildings, press SHIFT while giving
build orders. Units will execute each order, one at a time, in the sequence the orders were given. Press ALT instead of SHIFT if you want the Citizen to execute the new order before any previously given orders.
new_text:
To queue several consecutive move orders, press SHIFT while clicking the destinations.
To tell a Citi-snail to build a series of buildings, press SHIFT while giving
build orders. Units will execute each order, one at a time, in the sequence the orders were given. Press ALT instead of SHIFT if you want the Citi-snail to execute the new order before any previously given orders.

old_text:
Build a {University} to help you accumulate the #ICON4 {Knowledge} resource, which is useful for purchasing
research at the Library. Create {Scholars} at your University to increase Knowledge collection.
The more Scholars you have at your University, the faster you will accumulate Knowledge. Unlike other resources Knowledge can never be bought, sold, or exchanged.
new_text:
Build a {Paleo-versity} to help you accumulate the #ICON4 {Instinct} resource, which is useful for purchasing
research at the Fossil Record. Create {Bookworms} at your Paleo-versity to increase Instinct collection.
The more Bookworms you have at your Paleo-versity, the faster you will accumulate Instinct. Unlike other resources Instinct can never be bought, sold, or exchanged.

old_text:
Logistics, bureaucracy, and food supply have presented significant challenges to nations throughout history.
The more you build of a particular type of unit, the more each additional unit will cost and the longer it
will take to be created.
new_text:
Feeding, sheltering, and moving a growing swarm has challenged every lineage through deep time.
The more you build of a particular type of unit, the more each additional unit will cost and the longer it
will take to be created.

old_text: Use an {Attack Move} to have your troops move to a location while fighting any enemies they encounter along the way. With your troops selected, click the Attack button (or press A), and then click on a target map location. You can also simply CTRL + right-click on a map location to order an Attack Move.
new_text: Use an {Attack Move} to have your creatures move to a location while fighting any enemies they encounter along the way. With your creatures selected, click the Attack button (or press A), and then click on a target map location. You can also simply CTRL + right-click on a map location to order an Attack Move.

old_text:
To take control of the seas, your nation will need a {Dock}. Once you have a Dock and one #ICON27 Science technology, you can transport your ground units overseas--simply order them to move into the ocean,
and transport ships will automatically appear to pick them up. To land your troops simply move them back
onto land. When you have two #ICON26 Commerce
technologies, you can build Cities and Forts on other continents.
new_text:
To take control of the seas, your nation will need a {Tide-dock}. Once you have a Tide-dock and one #ICON27 Science technology, you can transport your ground units overseas--simply order them to move into the ocean,
and transport ships will automatically appear to pick them up. To land your creatures simply move them back
onto land. When you have two #ICON26 Commerce
technologies, you can build Cities and Reef Forts on other continents.

old_text:
Heavy ships such as Triremes are useful for achieving naval supremacy and destroying enemy shipping.
Light ships, such as Dromons, can move quickly to find and destroy enemy transports. In later ages you can build
Bombardment ships to attack land areas and Fire Ships and Submarines to counterattack against superior enemy
navies.
new_text:
Heavy swimmers such as Disc Triremes are useful for achieving naval supremacy and destroying enemy shipping.
Light swimmers, such as Fin-dromons, can move quickly to find and destroy enemy transports. In later ages you can build
Bombard swimmers to attack land areas and Fireships and Plesio-marines to counterattack against superior enemy
navies.

old_text: To overcome an enemy City, you need not raze it to the ground. Instead you may {capture} it by reducing its hit points to zero, eliminating any enemy Towers and Forts nearby, and achieving military superiority (i.e., having the most units, especially infantry units, in the vicinity). Once you have captured a city, a brief period is required to {assimilate} the new City into your nation.
new_text: To overcome an enemy City, you need not raze it to the ground. Instead you may {capture} it by reducing its hit points to zero, eliminating any enemy Stroma-towers and Reef Forts nearby, and achieving military superiority (i.e., having the most units, especially foot units, in the vicinity). Once you have captured a city, a brief period is required to {assimilate} the new City into your nation.

old_text: Building a {Temple} will increase the defensive strength of your City and will extend your National Borders. Upgrading the power of your religion at the Temple will increase these effects.
new_text: Building a {Amber Shrine} will increase the defensive strength of your City and will extend your National Borders. Upgrading the power of your religion at the Amber Shrine will increase these effects.

old_text: Supply Wagons support your troops, especially when they are in enemy territory. In enemy territory, Artillery and Siege Units reload much more quickly if they are near one of your Supply Wagons. Supply Wagons also protect your nearby troops from most forms of Attrition.
new_text: Horseshoe Supply Wagons support your creatures, especially when they are in enemy territory. In enemy territory, Siege Beasts reload much more quickly if they are near one of your Horseshoe Supply Wagons. Horseshoe Supply Wagons also protect your nearby creatures from most forms of Attrition.

old_text: Razing enemy buildings allows you to "plunder" resources. Attacking enemy caravans allows you to steal #ICON3 Wealth.
new_text: Razing enemy buildings allows you to "plunder" resources. Attacking enemy Roly-Poly Caravans allows you to steal #ICON3 Shells.

old_text: {Forts} and {Castles} are strong defensive positions, which also influence National Borders. They can also garrison military units, and can create Generals and Spies.
new_text: {Reef Forts} and {Coral Castles} are strong defensive positions, which also influence National Borders. They can also garrison military units, and can create General Tua-tactics and Chamele-spies.

old_text: Garrisoning military units inside Forts, Castles, Towers, and Cities protects the units from damage and increases the attack value of the building. To garrison military units in a building, select the military units, left-click the {Garrison} button, then left-click the building. Units can also garrison inside of the kind of building that produced them (e.g., Barracks, Dock, Siege Factory). Units garrisoned in buildings are gradually healed or repaired.
new_text: Garrisoning military units inside Reef Forts, Coral Castles, Stroma-towers, and Cities protects the units from damage and increases the attack value of the building. To garrison military units in a building, select the military units, left-click the {Garrison} button, then left-click the building. Units can also garrison inside of the kind of building that produced them (e.g., Burrow-acks, Tide-dock, Rockfall Works). Units garrisoned in buildings are gradually healed or repaired.

old_text: Spies can be used to {Bribe} enemy units to convert to your side. They can also recruit {Informers} among enemy buildings and troops, and employ {Counterintelligence} to destroy enemy Spies and remove enemy Informers.
new_text: Chamele-spies can be used to {Bribe} enemy units to convert to your side. They can also recruit {Informers} among enemy buildings and creatures, and employ {Counterintelligence} to destroy enemy Chamele-spies and remove enemy Informers.

old_text:
Generals can enhance the value of their troops in combat. Positioning them near their troops provides an increased combat value. Generals can order a {Forced March} temporarily increasing the speed of all of their
troops. They can place their forces in {Ambush} hiding their forces from enemy units for a period
of time. They can {Entrench} infantry to protect them from much enemy fire, and they can create {Decoy} units
to distract and confuse the enemy.
new_text:
General Tua-tactics can enhance the value of their creatures in combat. Positioning them near their creatures provides an increased combat value. General Tua-tactics can order a {Forced March} temporarily increasing the speed of all of their
creatures. They can place their forces in {Ambush} hiding their forces from enemy units for a period
of time. They can {Entrench} ground creatures to protect them from much enemy fire, and they can create {Decoy} units
to distract and confuse the enemy.

old_text: Press the default hotkey {L} to select one of your Libraries. A quick double-tap will center on the Library, and a triple-tap will zoom. Repeatedly pressing {L} without double-tapping will cycle you through all of your libraries. Other building types have similar keys, such as {U} for University, {N} for Market, and {C} for City.
new_text: Press the default hotkey {L} to select one of your Fossil Records. A quick double-tap will center on the Fossil Record, and a triple-tap will zoom. Repeatedly pressing {L} without double-tapping will cycle you through all of your Fossil Records. Other building types have similar keys, such as {U} for Paleo-versity, {N} for Shell Exchange, and {C} for City.

old_text:
To control the formation of your selected troops, right-click and hold where you want them to go, and then while
still holding down the right mouse button left-click to choose a formation. You can also drag while holding down
the right mouse button to change the facing. Roll the mouse wheel during the process to stretch/compress the
formation; use the arrow keys to fine tune the position of the formation.
new_text:
To control the formation of your selected creatures, right-click and hold where you want them to go, and then while
still holding down the right mouse button left-click to choose a formation. You can also drag while holding down
the right mouse button to change the facing. Roll the mouse wheel during the process to stretch/compress the
formation; use the arrow keys to fine tune the position of the formation.

old_text: You can use the Rally Point button to control where new units from your buildings (e.g., City, Barracks, Stable) go. With the building selected, click the Rally Point button (or press R), then click where you want new troops to go. You can hold down the SHIFT key while placing rally points to place multiple rally points for a single building (units will traverse them in the order you lay them).
new_text: You can use the Rally Point button to control where new units from your buildings (e.g., City, Burrow-acks, Stampede Pen) go. With the building selected, click the Rally Point button (or press R), then click where you want new creatures to go. You can hold down the SHIFT key while placing rally points to place multiple rally points for a single building (units will traverse them in the order you lay them).

old_text: The easiest way to launch planes from an Airbase is to select the base and then {right-click} where you want the planes to go. One plane (if available) will launch each time you right-click. You can also {SHIFT + right-click} to launch all available planes at the same time. With either method, planes will look for appropriate enemy targets to attack near the target location. Other options include {CTRL + right-click} to launch specifically a Bomber and {ALT + right-click} to launch specifically a Fighter; either can be combined with {SHIFT} to launch all of that type of aircraft.
new_text: The easiest way to launch flyers from a Cliff Roost is to select the base and then {right-click} where you want the flyers to go. One flyer (if available) will launch each time you right-click. You can also {SHIFT + right-click} to launch all available flyers at the same time. With either method, flyers will look for appropriate enemy targets to attack near the target location. Other options include {CTRL + right-click} to launch specifically a Bomb-coatlus and {ALT + right-click} to launch specifically a Fight-anodon; either can be combined with {SHIFT} to launch all of that type of flyers.

old_text: Build a missile at a Silo, then launch the missile by selecting the Silo and {right-clicking} the target.
new_text: Build a meteor at an Impact Silo, then launch the meteor by selecting the Impact Silo and {right-clicking} the target.

old_text:
If your nation has reached the #ICON34 Information Age and you have researched {all} technologies at the Library,
you will be able to research powerful {Future Technology}.
new_text:
If your nation has reached the #ICON34 Cenozoic Rise and you have researched {all} technologies at the Fossil Record,
you will be able to research powerful {Future Technology}.

old_text:
To build a Wonder of the World, select a Citizen and click the {Wonders} button. Two additional Wonders become available for each Age your nation advances. Once one nation builds a particular Wonder, such as the Pyramids, no other nations may construct that Wonder. Wonders provide special unique powers to your nation, and in some
games, help you achieve a {Wonder Victory}.
new_text:
To build a Wonder of the World, select a Citi-snail and click the {Wonders} button. Two additional Wonders become available for each Age your nation advances. Once one nation builds a particular Wonder, such as the Great Stroma-mids, no other nations may construct that Wonder. Wonders provide special unique powers to your nation, and in some
games, help you achieve a {Wonder Victory}.

old_text:
When an unfinished building (or a building under repair) is attacked by ground units, any Citizens working
on that building are damaged as well and will flee from the building.
new_text:
When an unfinished building (or a building under repair) is attacked by ground units, any Citi-snails working
on that building are damaged as well and will flee from the building.

old_text: Some buildings provide a special bonus when constructed. For instance, building a new Market provides a one-time #ICON3 Wealth bonus. Similarly, when the Mongols build a new Stable they gain free Ranged Cavalry units. However, these bonuses accrue only when the new building increases the nation's all time high total of that building--so if the Market (or Stable, etc) replaces one which was destroyed or voluntarily razed, no bonus applies.
new_text: Some buildings provide a special bonus when constructed. For instance, building a new Shell Exchange provides a one-time #ICON3 Shells bonus. Similarly, when the Veloci-Horde builds a new Stampede Pen they gain free Ranged Runners units. However, these bonuses accrue only when the new building increases the nation's all time high total of that building--so if the Shell Exchange (or Stampede Pen, etc) replaces one which was destroyed or voluntarily razed, no bonus applies.

old_text:
You cannot see #ICON6 {Oil} fields until your nation reaches the #ICON32 Industrial Age. Once you find Oil fields, you can
build {Oil Wells} either on land or at sea. Build {Refineries} to increase Oil Well output throughout your
nation.
new_text:
You cannot see #ICON6 {Oil} fields until your nation reaches the #ICON32 Jurassic Heights. Once you find Oil fields, you can
build {Tar Pits} either on land or at sea. Build {Bog-fineries} to increase Tar Pit output throughout your
nation.

old_text: To select all units (or buildings) anywhere on the map that match the type currently selected, press HOME. For example, if you have selected a Citizen, pressing HOME will select all Citizens anywhere in the game.
new_text: To select all units (or buildings) anywhere on the map that match the type currently selected, press HOME. For example, if you have selected a Citi-snail, pressing HOME will select all Citi-snails anywhere in the game.

old_text: [Thrones and Patriots] Senates are new buildings in Rise of Nations: Thrones and Patriots. They can be constructed after you reach the Classical Age. Senates perform three major functions:  <BULLET/> The City where you build your Senate becomes your Capital. <BULLET/> At the Senate you can research Governments that provide additional benefits to your nation. <BULLET/> When you research a Government, you receive a Patriot unit to assist you in battle.
new_text: [Thrones and Patriots] Herd Senates can be built once you reach the Cambrian Explosion. Herd Senates perform three major functions:  <BULLET/> The City where you build your Herd Senate becomes your Capital. <BULLET/> At the Herd Senate you can research Governments that provide additional benefits to your nation. <BULLET/> When you research a Government, you receive a Patriot unit to assist you in battle.

old_text: [Thrones and Patriots] Patriots are special Generals that are automatically created at the Senate when you have researched a Government. Each new Government you research will generate a different Patriot, each with specific powers. Some of the powers include healing nearby units, decreasing the time needed to assimilate an enemy City, decreasing the build time of your buildings nearby, and other effects.
new_text: [Thrones and Patriots] Patriots are special leaders that are automatically created at the Herd Senate when you have researched a Government. Each new Government you research will generate a different Patriot, each with specific powers. Some of the powers include healing nearby units, decreasing the time needed to assimilate an enemy City, decreasing the build time of your buildings nearby, and other effects.

old_text: [Thrones and Patriots] If your Patriot is killed in battle, another Patriot will come to your aid from the Senate. If your Capital is captured when your Patriot dies, he will reappear in a nearby city.
new_text: [Thrones and Patriots] If your Patriot is killed in battle, another Patriot will come to your aid from the Herd Senate. If your Capital is captured when your Patriot dies, he will reappear in a nearby city.

old_text:
[Thrones and Patriots] Can't find your Patriot? There's a new "Find Patriot" button below the "Find Military" button to the left of the minimap. Pressing
it once will find your Patriot; each subsequent press will find other Generals under your control.
new_text:
[Thrones and Patriots] Can't find your Patriot? There's a new "Find Patriot" button below the "Find Military" button to the left of the minimap. Pressing
it once will find your Patriot; each subsequent press will find other leaders under your control.
